draft.title: Where Australia's water is
card: Australia is the driest inhabited continent. Only Antarctica is drier, and no one lives there permanently.
Most rain falls on the north and east coasts and in Tasmania. Much of the inland gets little rain, so water on the surface there is scarce.
Groundwater is water stored in the soil and rock under the ground. Large stores of it lie under the inland.
The Great Artesian Basin is one of these stores. It lies under parts of Queensland, South Australia, New South Wales and the Northern Territory.
draft.remember: Most rain falls on the north and east coasts and in Tasmania, while large stores of groundwater lie under the dry inland.

a.q: Which area of Australia gets most of its rain?
opts: The north and east coasts and Tasmania
The middle of the continent
Every area gets about the same
The dry inland plains
a.why: Most rain falls on the north and east coasts and in Tasmania, while much of the inland gets little. Large stores of water do lie under the inland, but that is groundwater, not rain falling there.
a.clue: Much of Australia's centre is very dry.

b.q: Ben lives in a dry town in western Queensland. A visitor asks where a large store of water might lie near the town. What should Ben say?
opts: In groundwater stored in rock under the inland
In a large lake on the surface that stays full
In inland rivers that run high all year round
In a big dam filled by the town's own rainfall
b.why: Large stores of groundwater lie under the inland, and the Great Artesian Basin lies under parts of Queensland. The inland gets little rain, so its surface water is scarce, which rules out a lake that stays full, rivers running high all year or a dam filled by local rain.
b.clue: Little rain means little water stays on the surface.

a.best: The north and east coasts and Tasmania

b.best: In groundwater stored in rock under the inland

problems.detail: The right option is the longest and the only one naming specific places, and it repeats the remember line word for word, so a student could pick it without knowing the idea. Two distractors ('The middle of the continent' and 'The dry inland plains') say much the same thing, which weakens the choice.
'Which area of Australia gets most of its rain?' is ambiguous: 'its' could mean the area's own rain rather than Australia's rain. 'Which part of Australia gets the most rain?' would be clearer.

proposal.title: Australia's rainfall and water resources
card: Australia is the driest inhabited continent. Only Antarctica is drier, and no one lives there permanently.
Most rain falls on the north and east coasts and in Tasmania. Much of the inland is arid, meaning very dry, so water on the surface there is scarce.
Groundwater is water stored in the soil and rock under the ground. Large stores of it lie under the inland.
The Great Artesian Basin is one of these stores. It lies under parts of Queensland, South Australia, New South Wales and the Northern Territory.
proposal.remember: Australia's water is unevenly spread: wet coasts in the north, east and Tasmania, a dry inland with groundwater below.

a.q: Why is Australia's water described as unevenly spread?
opts: Some coasts get plenty of rain, but the inland gets little
The inland gets plenty of rain, but the coasts get little
Rain falls evenly, but some states use far more water
Australia gets less rain than every other continent
a.why: Unevenly spread means different places get very different amounts. The north and east coasts and Tasmania get most of the rain, while much of the inland is arid. The last option is about the total amount, not where it falls, and it is also wrong, because Antarctica is drier.
a.clue: Think about where the rain falls, not how much falls in total.

In a big dam filled by the town's own rainfall
b.why: Large stores of groundwater lie under the inland, and the Great Artesian Basin lies under parts of Queensland. The inland gets little rain, so its surface water is scarce, which rules out a lake that stays full, rivers running high all year or a dam filled by local rain.
b.clue: Little rain means little water stays on the surface.
